title: 第2章 废渣当宝贝？
novel_title: 凡人修仙：从废器房杂役开始
content_zh:
炉火烧了一整日，陈青山才把那块巴掌大的废渣带回小屋。

    他没有点灯。门闩一落，先把破布塞进窗缝，又贴着门听了好一会儿。

    院里只有炉灰被风卷过的沙沙声，没人走动，没人说话，废器房那些杂役累了一天，这会儿睡得跟死猪一样。

    袖口里，那粒米大的精铁屑还在；怀里，那块巴掌大的废铁渣也在。

    昨夜在废器库，他只敢试一片锈皮，不是不想试大的，是灵力已经见底，真晕在库房，第二天就得被铁三爷剥皮。

    所以他忍了一整日。白天在破炉前粗熔废料，分拣残片，挨张猛两句冷嘲，把这块废渣一直贴身藏着，等到收工、炉火熄尽，才敢关门。

    昨夜那一粒，是证明。眼前这一块，是续命。现在只剩一天一夜。

    五十斤精铁，炼不出来，铁三爷照样按着他的脑袋扣口粮；炼得出来，这个月才不用饿着肚子熬炉。

    陈青山把废铁渣攥在掌心，意识沉入识海。那口青铜鼎还悬在那里，古旧，安静，炉盖上“炼宝”两个字沉在暗光里。

    他没敢多想，只在心里压了一句：“试块大的。”

    心念一动，掌心忽然一轻，废铁渣没了。

    下一瞬，鼎火腾地亮起，陈青山整个人一抖，体内那点灵力像被一根细管牵住，从丹田里一丝丝往鼎里淌。

    不是一口抽空，可那种被慢慢掏走的滋味，比疼还磨人。

    鼎火卷着废渣翻动，灰黑杂质一层层浮起来，又一层层被火吞掉，剩下的东西越缩越小，越缩越亮。

    小半个时辰后，他后背已经沁出薄汗，丹田像个漏底的水缸，眼看着就要见底。

    天边泛白时，鼎火终于灭了。一小块东西飞出鼎，落进掌心。

    精铁。陈青山掂了掂，二两多。半斤废渣，正常熔炼撑死出四钱，这一炉却出了二两多，足足翻了好几倍，更要紧的是成色，银白，透亮，几乎找不着一丝杂质，比他在破炉上熬一整天的货还干净。

    成了。这鼎是真货。

    可他第一反应不是笑，而是抓了把冷灰，往那块银白上一抹。亮色压下去，看着就跟刚从废炉里扒出来的灰料一个样。

    好东西太亮，留不住命，练气一层的废材突然拿出雪亮精铁，不是发财，是找死。

    陈青山盯着掌心那块灰扑扑的精铁，慢慢想明白一件事。

    这鼎真正狠的地方，不是替他从头熔废器，以他练气一层那点灵力，一天撑死三四炉，光这样炼也凑不齐五十斤。它狠在，专啃别人嫌费劲、嫌脏、根本不愿碰的废渣烂料。

    白天，他照常在破炉上粗熔，让所有人看见他在干活。

    晚上，再把那些杂质最重、最难炼、别人扔在角落里不碰的东西丢进鼎里收尾。差料变好料，废渣补斤两。

    铁三爷罚他清一夜废器库，自以为往死里逼，如今看，倒像是亲手把粮仓门给他推开了。

    陈青山把那块精铁收进炉灰盆里，嘴角压了又压，没压住。老东西，这回怕是要失算了。

    接下来这一日一夜，他几乎没合眼。白天守着破炉装样子，火光遮着脸，汗顺着下巴往下滴，旁人只当这废材被逼急了，头一回肯拼命；夜里关门落闩，一炉接一炉地试。

    铁多的料鼎火稳，杂质太重的，先用明炉烧一遍，再入鼎，能省不少灵力。这些没人教他，全是一炉一炉拿命试出来的。

    最后一夜，灵力实在跟不上，他盯着袋里剩下的三颗辟谷丹看了半天。

    吃一颗，就少一颗；不吃，这炉撑不过去。

    陈青山咬牙捏碎一颗吞下，借着那点丹力，硬把鼎火续住。三颗口粮，少了一颗。值。
content_en:
The fire burned for a whole day before Chen Qingshan brought the palm-sized piece of waste back to the hut.

    He didn't light the lamp. As soon as the door latch fell, he stuffed the rag into the crack of the window and then leaned against the door to listen for a long time.

    There was only the rustle of ashes blown by the wind in the courtyard. No one moved or talked. The handymen in the scrap room were tired all day and now slept like dead pigs.

    In the cuffs, the fine iron filings the size of a rice are still there; in the arms, the scrap iron slag the size of a palm is also there.

    Last night in the scrap weapon warehouse, he only dared to try a piece of rust skin. It was not that he didn't want to try a big one, but because his spiritual power had bottomed out. He fainted in the warehouse and had to be peeled off by Master Tie San the next day.

    So he endured it all day. During the day, he roughly smelted scraps in front of the broken furnace, sorted the scraps, and received a few sneers from Zhang Meng. He kept the scraps close to his body until the work was done and the fire was extinguished before he dared to close the door.

    The pill last night was proof. The piece in front of me is to extend my life. Now there is only one day and one night left.

    If he couldn't refine fifty kilograms of refined iron, Mr. Tie San would still press his head to deduct rations; if he could refine it, he wouldn't have to go through the furnace hungry this month.

    Chen Qingshan held the scrap metal in his palms and his consciousness sank into the sea of ​​consciousness. The bronze cauldron is still hanging there, old and quiet, and the words "Lian Bao" on the furnace lid are lost in the dark light.

    He didn't dare to think too much, he just said in his mind: "Try a big one."

    As soon as I thought about it, my palm suddenly lightened, and the scrap iron slag was gone.

    The next moment, the cauldron lit up with fire, and Chen Qingshan trembled. The spiritual power in his body seemed to be held by a thin tube, flowing from his dantian into the cauldron.

    It's not like taking it all away in one go, but the feeling of being slowly taken away is more excruciating than the pain.

    The cauldron fire rolled up the waste residue, and the gray and black impurities floated up layer by layer, and were swallowed up layer by layer by the fire. The remaining things shrank smaller and smaller, and shrunk and shone brighter.

    Less than half an hour later, a thin layer of sweat broke out on his back, and his dantian was like a leaky water tank, about to bottom out.

    When the sky turned white, the cauldron fire finally went out. A small piece of something flew out of the cauldron and fell into the palm of my hand.

    Fine iron. Chen Qingshan weighed it and found two or two more. Half a kilogram of waste slag, which can be smelted normally for four cents, but this furnace yielded more than two taels, which was several times higher. What's more important was the color. It was silvery white and translucent, with almost no trace of impurities. It was cleaner than the product he had simmered in a broken furnace for a whole day.

    It’s done. This tripod is genuine.

    But his first reaction was not to laugh, but to grab a handful of cold ashes and rub it on the silvery white. When the bright color is pressed down, it looks like the ashes just pulled out of the abandoned furnace.

    A good thing is too bright to survive. If a useless person at the first level of Qi training suddenly comes up with sharp iron, he is not making a fortune, but seeking death.

    Chen Qingshan stared at the dusty piece of fine iron in his palm, and slowly figured out one thing.

    The real ruthlessness of this cauldron is not that it melts scraps for him from scratch. With his spiritual power at the first level of Qi training, he can hold up three or four furnaces a day. He can't even make up to fifty kilograms by just doing this. It is ruthless and specializes in chewing up scraps that others find too laborious, too dirty, and simply don't want to touch.

    During the day, he continued to smelt crudely on the broken furnace, letting everyone see him working.

    In the evening, throw the items with the heaviest impurities, the most difficult to refine, and those that others have left in the corner without touching them into the cauldron to finish. Poor materials are turned into good materials, and waste residues are replenished.

    Tie Sanye punished him to clean out the abandoned weapon warehouse overnight, thinking that he was going to death, but now it looks like he pushed open the granary door with his own hands.

    Chen Qingshan put the piece of fine iron into the ash basin and pressed the corner of his mouth again and again, but failed to hold it down. Old guy, I'm afraid I'm going to make a mistake this time.

    For the next day and night, he barely slept a wink. During the day, he stood by the broken stove and pretended, with the firelight covering his face and sweat dripping down his chin. Others just thought that this good-for-nothing was cornered and he was willing to fight for the first time; at night, he closed the door and unlatched it, and tried one stove after another.

    Materials with a lot of iron will make the cauldron stable in fire, but materials with too many impurities can be burned in an open furnace before being put into the cauldron, which can save a lot of spiritual energy. No one taught him these things; he learned them through trial and error.

    On the last night, his spiritual power really couldn't keep up, so he stared at the three Bigu Pills left in his bag for a long time.

    If you eat one, you will lose one; if you don't eat, the furnace will not survive.

    Chen Qingshan gritted his teeth, crushed one and swallowed it, and with that bit of elixir power, he continued to hold the cauldron fire. Three rations, one missing. value.
